title: Compare standard deviation or spread without calculating
subtitle: One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread · 3 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **3 of the official questions in One-variable data: Distributions and measures of center and spread are this one** — 0 Easy, 3 Medium, 0 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get two histograms or dot plots, or answer choices that are lists (often all symmetric about the same center), and must say which is smaller or larger or whether they are equal.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Find the center of each set.
- It is often identical by symmetry.
- 2) Ask which set has more of its values bunched near the center and fewer out at the extremes; that one has the smaller SD.
- 3) A shifted but identical shape means equal SD.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Enter each list and use stdev() to confirm if you are unsure, but the visual 'distance from center' judgment is faster and is what the question tests.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You judge spread by range alone or by the number of distinct values instead of how much data sits far from the mean.
Or you think two identically shaped histograms at different locations have different SDs.

sections.heading: You are losing these
